newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly up in range trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly up in range trade.

text.p: *Central Bank seen as net seller at 26.285
The Philippine peso closed a notch higher on Tuesday at 26.284 to the dollar from 26.285 on arbitrage play, traders said.
"The market was just range-trading," a foreign bank dealer said.

Dealers said banks were selling their dollars for same-day delivery to take advantage of the higher interest premium of the peso over the dollar. At the same time, banks were also buying the dollars for next-day delivery to recover the dollars they sold.
Dealers said the Central Bank was a net seller of dollars in the market to meet some demand from foreign investors departing out of the country's equities market.
One dealer estimated the Central Bank sold a net of $21.5 million at 26.285.
The day's average was at 26.284 from 26.283, with volume falling to $95.50 million from $119.67 million.
The peso just moved within a close band from 26.286 to 26.281.
